title: What is the rarest color in nature? - Victoria Hwang
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】自然界中最稀有的顏色是什麼？ - 黃維多利亞（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Every color you see in front of you can be found in nature.
cues.en: Every color you see in front of you can be found in nature.
cues.zh: 你眼前的所有顏色， 都能在大自然中找到。 有些植物、動物、礦物， 含有你能想像到的幾乎所有顏色。

cues.text: Some plant, animal, or mineral bears almost every hue imaginable.
cues.en: Some plant, animal, or mineral bears almost every hue imaginable.
cues.zh: 有些植物、動物、礦物， 含有你能想像到的幾乎所有顏色。

cues.text: But which of these colors are you least likely to see in the natural world?
cues.en: But which of these colors are you least likely to see in the natural world?
cues.zh: 但在這些顏色之中， 哪一種顏色最難在自然中發現？

cues.text: There are two factors that drive the rarity of color in nature:
cues.en: There are two factors that drive the rarity of color in nature:
cues.zh: 自然顏色的稀有度， 主要由兩個因素決定：

cues.text: physics and evolution.
cues.en: physics and evolution.
cues.zh: 物理和演化。

cues.text: Let’s start with physics.
cues.en: Let’s start with physics.
cues.zh: 讓我們先來看看物理學。

cues.text: Colors are generated when wavelengths of light interact with objects,
cues.en: Colors are generated when wavelengths of light interact with objects,
cues.zh: 顏色是光的波長 和物體表面互動的結果。

cues.text: and most of the colors you’ve seen outside a screen were produced in one of two ways.
cues.en: and most of the colors you’ve seen outside a screen were produced in one of two ways.
cues.zh: 顏色是光的波長 和物體表面互動的結果。 你在螢幕外看見的大多數顏色， 由兩種方式產生。 就基於吸收而產生的顏色來說，

cues.text: In absorption-based colors, certain wavelengths are absorbed by an object, while others are not.
cues.en: In absorption-based colors, certain wavelengths are absorbed by an object, while others are not.
cues.zh: 就基於吸收而產生的顏色來說， 物體會吸收特定波長的光波， 而反射其他波長的光波。

cues.text: The result is a matte final color generated by these leftover light waves.
cues.en: The result is a matte final color generated by these leftover light waves.
cues.zh: 這些被反射的光波彼此混合， 產生最終顯示的顏色。

cues.text: Most naturally occurring colors fall into this category, including those of many fruits and flowers.
cues.en: Most naturally occurring colors fall into this category, including those of many fruits and flowers.
cues.zh: 大多數的自然顏色都是這樣產生， 包括許多水果和花卉的顏色。

cues.text: Plants are full of compounds called pigments that absorb light waves as part of photosynthesis,
cues.en: Plants are full of compounds called pigments that absorb light waves as part of photosynthesis,
cues.zh: 植物飽含名為「光合色素」的化合物， 用來吸收光線，作為光合作用的一環。 光合作用能將陽光轉化為能量。

cues.text: the process by which they convert sunlight into energy.
cues.en: the process by which they convert sunlight into energy.
cues.zh: 光合作用能將陽光轉化為能量。

cues.text: While different plants have evolved different pigments that result in different colors,
cues.en: While different plants have evolved different pigments that result in different colors,
cues.zh: 由於不同植物演化出不同的色素， 所以它們呈現的顏色也不同，

cues.text: higher energy wavelengths are more easily absorbed than lower energy ones.
cues.en: higher energy wavelengths are more easily absorbed than lower energy ones.
cues.zh: 較高能量的波長， 比較低能量的光更容易被吸收。

cues.text: And blue light has some of the highest energy wavelengths in the visible spectrum.
cues.en: And blue light has some of the highest energy wavelengths in the visible spectrum.
cues.zh: 而在可見光中， 藍光是能量最高的光波之一。

cues.text: Numerous pigments have evolved to absorb blue light, including chlorophyll, which absorbs blue and red wavelengths
cues.en: Numerous pigments have evolved to absorb blue light, including chlorophyll, which absorbs blue and red wavelengths
cues.zh: 許多光合色素演化出吸收藍光的功能， 例如能吸收紅光和藍光的葉綠素， 製造出大自然的標誌性綠色。

cues.text: to produce nature’s trademark green.
cues.en: to produce nature’s trademark green.
cues.zh: 製造出大自然的標誌性綠色。

cues.text: However, green light is still fairly energetic, and the most common class of pigments evolved to absorb these wavelengths
cues.en: However, green light is still fairly energetic, and the most common class of pigments evolved to absorb these wavelengths
cues.zh: 但是，綠光的能量也不低， 因此最常見的光合色素也都演化出 吸收綠光的功能。

cues.text: as well.
cues.en: as well.
cues.zh: 吸收綠光的功能。

cues.text: There are over 1,100 types of carotenoids, pigments which absorb high energy blue and green light,
cues.en: There are over 1,100 types of carotenoids, pigments which absorb high energy blue and green light,
cues.zh: 有超過 1100 種類胡蘿蔔素， 這是一種能吸收高能量的藍光與綠光， 同時反射低能量的 紅光與黃光的光合色素。

cues.text: while leaving behind the lower energy red and yellow light.
cues.en: while leaving behind the lower energy red and yellow light.
cues.zh: 同時反射低能量的 紅光與黃光的光合色素。

cues.text: While carotenoids are present in most green plants, they only become visible each fall when chlorophyll gets broken down
cues.en: While carotenoids are present in most green plants, they only become visible each fall when chlorophyll gets broken down
cues.zh: 雖然幾乎每種植物都含有類胡蘿蔔素， 但要到每年秋天，植物為了 儲備過冬能量而分解葉綠素時，

cues.text: to save energy for the winter.
cues.en: to save energy for the winter.
cues.zh: 但要到每年秋天，植物為了 儲備過冬能量而分解葉綠素時， 我們才能看見它們的顏色。

cues.text: But whether they’re working alone or side by side, these pigments absorb blue light in virtually all plants.
cues.en: But whether they’re working alone or side by side, these pigments absorb blue light in virtually all plants.
cues.zh: 但無論這些光合色素 是分工合作，或是單打獨鬥， 幾乎所有植物都會吸收藍光。

cues.text: Even fruits and flowers that appear blue actually have pigments that are red or purple,
cues.en: Even fruits and flowers that appear blue actually have pigments that are red or purple,
cues.zh: 就算是看似藍色的水果或花朵， 其實也含有紅色或紫色的色素， 並只在特定化學條件下才會變成藍色。

cues.text: and only truly turn blue under specific chemical conditions.
cues.en: and only truly turn blue under specific chemical conditions.
cues.zh: 並只在特定化學條件下才會變成藍色。

cues.text: So, is blue the rarest color in nature?
cues.en: So, is blue the rarest color in nature?
cues.zh: 所以藍色是自然中最稀有的顏色嗎？

cues.text: Not quite.
cues.en: Not quite.
cues.zh: 還不能下定論。

cues.text: Absorption is just one of the two main ways light generates color.
cues.en: Absorption is just one of the two main ways light generates color.
cues.zh: 吸收只是光產生顏色的其中一種方法。

cues.text: In the second method, some wavelengths are scattered and amplified—
cues.en: In the second method, some wavelengths are scattered and amplified—
cues.zh: 第二種方法中， 某些光波被散射、放大， 凌駕於其他光波之上， 決定了物體最終的顏色。

cues.text: overpowering the others to determine an object's final color.
cues.en: overpowering the others to determine an object's final color.
cues.zh: 凌駕於其他光波之上， 決定了物體最終的顏色。

cues.text: These structural colors occur because some objects around us are made of microscopic particles
cues.en: These structural colors occur because some objects around us are made of microscopic particles
cues.zh: 這些結構色之所以產生， 是因為我們周遭的 某些東西由微粒組成， 能產生奈米結構，和可見光相互作用。

cues.text: which can form nanostructures that interfere with visible light.
cues.en: which can form nanostructures that interfere with visible light.
cues.zh: 是因為我們周遭的 某些東西由微粒組成， 能產生奈米結構，和可見光相互作用。

cues.text: For example, this feather has no blue pigments in it.
cues.en: For example, this feather has no blue pigments in it.
cues.zh: 例如，這根羽毛並不含藍色的色素。 但光照射在羽毛上時， 羽毛奈米結構中的電子

cues.text: But when light strikes it, the electrons within its nanostructure
cues.en: But when light strikes it, the electrons within its nanostructure
cues.zh: 但光照射在羽毛上時， 羽毛奈米結構中的電子 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。

cues.text: vibrate at the same frequency as the wave.
cues.en: vibrate at the same frequency as the wave.
cues.zh: 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波，

cues.text: This makes the particles send out a new wave with the same frequency,
cues.en: This makes the particles send out a new wave with the same frequency,
cues.zh: 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波，

cues.text: starting a chain reaction that amplifies and scatters blue light.
cues.en: starting a chain reaction that amplifies and scatters blue light.
cues.zh: 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波， 開始一段能放大、 折射藍光的連鎖反應。

cues.text: Nanostructures of various shapes and sizes scatter different wavelengths,
cues.en: Nanostructures of various shapes and sizes scatter different wavelengths,
cues.zh: 不同形狀和尺寸的奈米結構， 會折射出不同波長， 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波，

cues.text: but they typically scatter high-energy wavelengths most easily—
cues.en: but they typically scatter high-energy wavelengths most easily—
cues.zh: 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波， 讓藍光成了最常見的「構造色」。

cues.text: making blue the most common structural color.
cues.en: making blue the most common structural color.
cues.zh: 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波， 讓藍光成了最常見的「構造色」。

cues.text: Meanwhile, low-energy wavelengths like red are only weakly scattered.
cues.en: Meanwhile, low-energy wavelengths like red are only weakly scattered.
cues.zh: 而紅色這種低能量的光波， 折射力道通常很弱。

cues.text: Even when something evolves specific nanostructures that strongly scatter red light
cues.en: Even when something evolves specific nanostructures that strongly scatter red light
cues.zh: 就算有東西演化出特別的奈米結構， 能折射出強烈的紅光， 這些結構仍會和其他波長的光共振，

cues.text: they still resonate with other wavelengths, only appearing red at some angles of illumination and observation.
cues.en: they still resonate with other wavelengths, only appearing red at some angles of illumination and observation.
cues.zh: 這些結構仍會和其他波長的光共振， 只能以某些角度照明、觀察， 才能看見紅色。

cues.text: This gives us two contenders for nature’s rarest color:
cues.en: This gives us two contenders for nature’s rarest color:
cues.zh: 這讓我們看見自然界 最稀有顏色的兩個競爭者：

cues.text: absorption-based matte blues and structural iridescent reds.
cues.en: absorption-based matte blues and structural iridescent reds.
cues.zh: 因吸收混合出的藍色， 以及結構色中的紅色。

cues.text: Between these two, structural reds are much rarer.
cues.en: Between these two, structural reds are much rarer.
cues.zh: 以這兩者來說，結構色的紅色更稀有。

cues.text: Only a handful of animals and rocks scatter red light
cues.en: Only a handful of animals and rocks scatter red light
cues.zh: 只有少數動物和石頭能折射出紅光，

cues.text: and none of them scatter red light exclusively.
cues.en: and none of them scatter red light exclusively.
cues.zh: 但沒有一種物體能只折射出紅光。

cues.text: But since red and blue are rare in one way and common in another,
cues.en: But since red and blue are rare in one way and common in another,
cues.zh: 在兩種形成顏色的方式中，紅色 和藍色各是一種稀缺另一種普遍，

cues.text: we actually end up seeing both colors quite often.
cues.en: we actually end up seeing both colors quite often.
cues.zh: 在兩種形成顏色的方式中，紅色 和藍色各是一種稀缺另一種普遍， 因此我們仍能時常看見紅色與藍色。

cues.text: So what color is least likely to be generated in structural and absorption-based forms?
cues.en: So what color is least likely to be generated in structural and absorption-based forms?
cues.zh: 所以，究竟是哪種顏色最難製造， 不管是以結構色還是吸收色而言？

cues.text: The answer is violet.
cues.en: The answer is violet.
cues.zh: 答案是藍紫色。

cues.text: Not to be confused with purple, which is just a combination of red and blue light,
cues.en: Not to be confused with purple, which is just a combination of red and blue light,
cues.zh: 可別把它誤認成 紅光和藍光混合出的紫色。

cues.text: violet occupies a small portion of the visible light spectrum.
cues.en: violet occupies a small portion of the visible light spectrum.
cues.zh: 可別把它誤認成 紅光和藍光混合出的紫色。 藍紫光也是可見光譜裡的小小一員。

cues.text: There are only a few nanostructures precise enough to exclusively scatter violet light.
cues.en: There are only a few nanostructures precise enough to exclusively scatter violet light.
cues.zh: 只有少數夠精確的奈米結構， 才能特別散射出藍紫光。 藍紫光的能量比藍光更強，

cues.text: And violet wavelengths are even more energetic than blue ones, making them likely to be absorbed by pigment.
cues.en: And violet wavelengths are even more energetic than blue ones, making them likely to be absorbed by pigment.
cues.zh: 藍紫光的能量比藍光更強， 因此更容易被光合色素吸收。

cues.text: So if you ever stumble onto the iridescent violet wings
cues.en: So if you ever stumble onto the iridescent violet wings
cues.zh: 所以如果你碰巧看到 紫帝王蝶的藍紫色雙翅，

cues.text: of a purple emperor butterfly, take a second to appreciate one of nature’s rarest spectacles.
cues.en: of a purple emperor butterfly, take a second to appreciate one of nature’s rarest spectacles.
cues.zh: 紫帝王蝶的藍紫色雙翅， 就花點時間，欣賞 大自然中最獨特的奇觀吧。
